name: Grand Lake Stream (Indian Hill)
summary: Washington County, ME enclosed wooden tower built 1934 on Downeast Lakes Land Trust land; judged non-salvageable in 2025, now gone, with a July 2026 cleanup planned for a picnic site.
design: enclosed wooden fire tower; the land trust's news release, reproduced in the chapter's 2025 report, calls it the last remaining enclosed wooden fire tower in New England
status_note: Judged non-salvageable in 2025; the chapter report (data to 12/31/2025) said removal had not happened; a later land trust trail page calls the site former (now gone); exact removal date not found
agency: Maine Forest Service managed the tower; site on Downeast Lakes Land Trust property

access.note: Former site is beside the land trust's Tower Hill Trail, which it lists among its hikes; a public picnic site was planned, not confirmed as built

visit.drive_up: Park at the West Grand Lake Dam lot or along the extension of Tower Road
visit.trail_note: Tower Hill Trail runs near the former tower site; the tower itself is gone

events.note: Built in 1934 per the chapter's 2025 report and the land trust
Structural architects and Maine Cabin Masters contractors assessed the tower and found it non-salvageable; reported in the chapter's 2025 annual report (assessment date not given)
Land trust scheduled a volunteer cleanup of the former site for 07/10/2026 to turn it into a public picnic site
Exact removal date not found. The chapter report (data to 12/31/2025) says removal had not occurred; a later land trust page calls the site former (now gone)
